overall_summary: The channel has a very small sample size of views (all under 40) with negligible engagement across 10 videos. While absolute numbers are low, 'self respect' and digital/phone-related triggers (like deleting chats or unnamed numbers) show slight relative strength compared to abstract topics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on phone interactions like chat deletion and unnamed numbers (e.g., AfaLxMy6FMY, aNR94Xxn0yM) achieved the highest views (33 and 24).
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize modern, relatable digital micro-behaviors (typing and deleting, online status) over old-fashioned romantic clichés.

weak_patterns.evidence: Broad late-night or tea-drinking tropes (e.g., uIbMpCjVutQ, G0gKV1p3ZHc) received the lowest views (5 and 12).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic atmospheric setups and ground every story in an immediate, physical phone or text action.

next_video.concept: Seeing someone view your story after months of silence, and choosing to mute them instead of replying.
next_video.opening_direction: Notification pops up showing 'Seen by [Name]' on a broadcast or status after 6 months.
next_video.twist_direction: Instead of feeling excited or tempted to text back, you tap 'Mute' because your peace matters more than their temporary boredom.
next_video.reason: Previous successful posts like 'self respect' peaked when published during afternoon hours (around 13:45 UTC/IST test windows), tapping into mid-day scrolling behavior.

experiment: Testing if shifting from passive longing (waiting for texts) to active boundary-setting (muting/blocking) improves engagement on self-respect topics.
